items.claim: The row's continuity driver — one sustained address with no new addressee anywhere across Isa.57.3-Isa.57.13 — is byte-contested: the address switches from second-person masculine plural to second-person feminine singular inside the span, and a shared form whose only same-chapter pair straddles the row's closing seam is left undisclosed.
items.evidence: The opening run וְאַתֶּ֥ם קִרְבוּ הֵ֖נָּה בְּנֵ֣י עֹנְנָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.57.3) re-collates at byte tier, and its forms are plural: the imperative and the pronoun both address a masculine plural group, continued at oshb:Isa.57.4 by עַל מִי֙ תִּתְעַנָּ֔גוּ (byte tier) and by the plural pronoun later in that verse. oshb:Isa.57.5 carries no finite second-person form at all (a participial chain). From oshb:Isa.57.6 onward every second-person form in the span is feminine singular — שָׁפַ֥כְתְּ נֶ֨סֶךְ֙ הֶעֱלִ֣ית מִנְחָ֔ה (byte tier) — and that continues unbroken to the row's closing verse (the feminine-suffixed forms of oshb:Isa.57.13). So a hard grammatical addressee change sits at the oshb:Isa.57.4 | oshb:Isa.57.6 junction, and the row's own type description names only the feminine personification, i.e. only the second of the two addressees it treats as one. The rival cut the row does disclose (at web:Isa.57.11) lies wholly inside the feminine-singular stretch and is the weaker of the two candidates. Undisclosed cross-seam device: the form וְנִשָּׂ֔א at oshb:Isa.57.7 (of the high mountain the addressee climbs) and the same word at oshb:Isa.57.15 (of the enthroned speaker) are identical at accent-stripped tier and differ only in accent at byte tier; that form stands in 6 verses book-wide at accent-stripped tier (sweep: 6 verses — MT 2:2, 6:1, 39:6, 52:13, 57:7, 57:15), and MT 57:7/57:15 are its only two sites inside one chapter, straddling this row's own closing seam with no disclosure on this side. Verified true: the mark claim — no petuchah or setumah at MT 57:2, inside MT 57:3-13, or on MT 57:13 — matches the single-witness inventory, and no paseq or ketiv/qere object falls in the span either.

items.claim: The setumah the row cites for its opening byte-sits after MT 57:14, so it corroborates a cut at MT 57:14 | 57:15 — exactly where the span's only koh-amar frame stands — while the row's actual front-seam frame form is never quoted and the rival opening is never disclosed.
items.evidence: In the single-witness source the setumah seg is attached inside the MT 57:14 verse element, after that verse's words, so the break falls between MT 57:14 and MT 57:15 and not before MT 57:14. The convention is consistent across this stretch: the other three setumot here (MT 57:21, MT 58:14, MT 59:21) all sit at verse-ends that the surrounding units read as closes. The row's true front seam, MT 57:13 | 57:14, therefore carries no mark, and the mark it lists as opening evidence is span-internal. What sits at that seg is the span's only koh-amar frame: כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר רָ֣ם (oshb:Isa.57.15, byte tier), the koh-amar formula (sweep: 48 verses book-wide, skeleton tier; MT 57:15 is its only site inside MT 57:14-57:21), whose speaker here is named by epithet with no tetragrammaton anywhere in the verse. Two independent signals therefore converge on MT 57:15 as a rival opening, and the row discloses neither — its rejected alternative addresses only the closing pair. Separately, the row's own opening driver is a frame-based seam claim carried entirely on an English rendering: the speech-introduction form וְאָמַ֥ר (oshb:Isa.57.14, byte tier) is byte-present but never quoted. Verified true: paseq and a ketiv/qere note both stand at MT 57:19 in the single-witness inventory; the row's quoted run at that verse does avoid the doubled ketiv/qere token pair; and the comparison to oshb:Isa.48.22 is byte-exact — אֵ֣ין שָׁל֔וֹם אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהַ֖י לָרְשָׁעִֽים against אֵ֣ין שָׁל֔וֹם אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה לָרְשָׁעִֽים differ only in the divine-name token, and that phrase stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier). One imprecision in the frame-class grouping: oshb:Isa.57.15 and oshb:Isa.30.12 carry no tetragrammaton in the frame at all, but oshb:Isa.42.5 and oshb:Isa.51.22 both do carry it inside the frame, so the shared property as stated holds for only one of the three cited parallels, and oshb:Isa.21.6, the member with an intervening dative, is omitted.

items.claim: Both Hebrew splices reach byte tier at their cited verses, the mark disclosure is byte-correct at both edges and complete for the span, and the closing signature is a genuine three-site book-wide formula.
items.evidence: קְרָ֤א בְגָרוֹן֙ אַל תַּחְשֹׂ֔ךְ (oshb:Isa.58.1) and כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר (oshb:Isa.58.14) both re-collate at byte tier, and the space-for-maqaf spelling in the first run matches the staged extract's convention rather than being a transcription slip. The closing formula stands in exactly 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier — MT 1:20, MT 40:5, MT 58:14), so treating it as a formal signature at the row's close is byte-warranted rather than impressionistic. Mark claims check out against the single-witness inventory: setumah attached to MT 57:21 (break after that verse, i.e. this row's front seam) and setumah attached to MT 58:14 (this row's closing verse); no paseq, ketiv/qere, or special-letter object falls anywhere in MT 58:1-58:14, so the span's disclosure set is complete with nothing owed. The sabbath echo the row records is byte-present and spelling-distinct — שֹׁמֵ֤ר שַׁבָּת֙ at oshb:Isa.56.2 and אֶת שַׁבְּתוֹתַ֔י at oshb:Isa.56.4 against the prefixed forms at oshb:Isa.58.13 (byte tier) — and the row correctly confines it to prose texture rather than letting it argue a boundary. Noted without prejudice: the address alternates masculine singular at MT 58:1, masculine plural at MT 58:3-58:6 (קוֹלְכֶֽם, byte tier), and masculine singular again from MT 58:7 (הֲל֨וֹא פָרֹ֤ס לָֽרָעֵב֙ לַחְמֶ֔ךָ, byte tier), so the byte-hardest internal candidate is MT 58:6 | 58:7 rather than the pivot the row rejects; the row's continuity claim is anchored at MT 58:8 and MT 58:13, both continuous with MT 58:7, so it survives the check.

items.claim: The row's opening driver is a presentative particle that stands twice inside the immediately preceding span, so it is not seam-distinctive; and a two-site book-wide phrase on the row's own closing verse, plus a chapter-length salvation-root inclusio the row's own quote starts, are left undisclosed while the signal-class field is empty.
items.evidence: הֵ֛ן לֹֽא קָצְרָ֥ה יַד יְהוָ֖ה מֵֽהוֹשִׁ֑יעַ (oshb:Isa.59.1) re-collates at byte tier, but the same particle stands at oshb:Isa.58.3 (הֵ֣ן בְּי֤וֹם צֹֽמְכֶם֙, byte tier) and verse-initially at oshb:Isa.58.4 (הֵ֣ן לְרִ֤יב וּמַצָּה֙, byte tier), both inside the preceding unit; it is a presentative particle carrying no frame role at any of the three sites, so this row's boundary rests on the person turn and the tier-3 mark, not on the particle the rationale leads with. Undisclosed cross-seam device: the row's closing verse carries וְאֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּ֖ט בְּמַעְגְּלוֹתָ֑ם (oshb:Isa.59.8, byte tier), and that phrase stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier — MT 59:8 and MT 59:15); its partner sits at MT 59:15, so the pairing brackets the intervening material and bears directly on this row's own closing seam. Also undisclosed: the salvation root inside the row's own opening splice, מֵֽהוֹשִׁ֑יעַ, returns at oshb:Isa.59.16 (וַתּ֤וֹשַֽׁע) and oshb:Isa.59.17 (וְכ֥וֹבַע יְשׁוּעָ֖ה) (byte tier) — the salvation family, not the prophet's name, which shares consonants but not this order — an inclusio across MT ch 59 that runs straight through the row's closing seam. Finally, the signal-class field is left empty although the row's own drivers (assertion onset, addressee turn) both have taxonomy classes available, and the row's other disclosures are prose-only. Verified true: the masculine-plural address does run MT 59:2-3 and turns to third-person description at MT 59:4 (byte tier), and the mark claim is byte-correct — setumah attached to MT 58:14 (break after that verse, this row's front seam) with no mark, paseq, or ketiv/qere object anywhere inside MT 59:1-59:8.

items.claim: The row's sole boundary driver is a form-class claim about MT 59:10-59:12 asserted from English renderings with no pointed splice, and the two-site book-wide phrase that brackets the span at both its seams is undisclosed in either direction.
items.evidence: The underlying facts check out, so the defect is engagement rather than truth: MT 59:9-59:14 contains no vav-consecutive imperfect — נְגַֽשְׁשָׁ֤ה כַֽעִוְרִים֙ קִ֔יר and כָּשַׁ֤לְנוּ at oshb:Isa.59.10, כִּֽי רַבּ֤וּ פְשָׁעֵ֨ינוּ֙ and וַעֲוֺנֹתֵ֖ינוּ יְדַֽעֲנֽוּם at oshb:Isa.59.12, and וְהֻסַּ֤ג אָחוֹר֙ מִשְׁפָּ֔ט at oshb:Isa.59.14 (a vav plus perfect, not a vav-consecutive imperfect) all re-collate at byte tier — while oshb:Isa.59.15 opens וַתְּהִ֤י הָֽאֱמֶת֙ נֶעְדֶּ֔רֶת and continues וַיַּ֧רְא יְהוָ֛ה וַיֵּ֥רַע בְּעֵינָ֖יו (byte tier). But the row quotes Hebrew only for its opening verse; every enumerated form at MT 59:10, MT 59:11 and MT 59:12 is carried on a translation, and no morphology layer is staged, so the row's own load-bearing claim cannot be checked from the row itself. Undisclosed cross-seam device: וְאֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּ֖ט (oshb:Isa.59.8) and כִּֽי אֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּֽט (oshb:Isa.59.15) (byte tier) put the same phrase in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier), i.e. on the verse immediately before this row's front seam and on the verse immediately after its back seam — a bracket around this row's whole span that bears on both of its seams and is disclosed at neither. The same catchword is dense here: it stands in 40 verses book-wide (sweep: 40 verses, skeleton tier), 5 of them in MT ch 59 (59:8, 59:9, 59:11, 59:14, 59:15). Verified true: the mark disclosure is byte-correct — no petuchah, setumah, paseq, or ketiv/qere object falls at MT 59:8 | 59:9 or anywhere inside MT 59:9-59:14 in the single-witness inventory.

items.claim: The two distinct frame forms that carry the row's seam judgements at MT 59:20 and MT 59:21 are asserted from English only, where they read as one phrase, the narrative chain the row argues byte-terminates one verse before its prose carries it, and the catchwords crossing the row's closing seam are undisclosed.
items.evidence: The row's own three splices all re-collate at byte tier and its opening argument is the strongest in the cluster: וַתְּהִ֤י הָֽאֱמֶת֙ נֶעְדֶּ֔רֶת is itself a vav-consecutive imperfect and the chain continues וַיַּ֧רְא יְהוָ֛ה וַיֵּ֥רַע בְּעֵינָ֖יו (oshb:Isa.59.15, byte tier). But the decision not to close at web:Isa.59.20 turns on that verse's signature and the decision to hold web:Isa.59.21 turns on its doubled frame, and neither Hebrew form is quoted although both are byte-present: נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה at oshb:Isa.59.20 is the postpositive signature, while oshb:Isa.59.21 carries אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה twice — a different frame object — and the row's prose renders both with the same English words, so a reader cannot see from the row which formula stands where. The chain claim also overruns: it byte-runs MT 59:15, MT 59:16 and MT 59:17, whose last link is וַיַּ֥עַט (byte tier), and stops there — oshb:Isa.59.18's verbs are imperfect, כְּעַ֣ל יְשַׁלֵּ֔ם and גְּמ֥וּל יְשַׁלֵּֽם (byte tier) — so carrying the chain 'on through' MT 59:18 is not byte-supported. Undisclosed at the row's own closing seam: the light-and-rising root runs oshb:Isa.59.19 (וּמִמִּזְרַח שֶׁ֖מֶשׁ) straight into oshb:Isa.60.1 (זָרָֽח), oshb:Isa.60.2 and oshb:Isa.60.3 (byte tier) — 10 verses book-wide (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton tier) of which four run consecutively across this seam; and the redeemer noun at oshb:Isa.59.20 returns suffixed at oshb:Isa.60.16 while the salvation noun at oshb:Isa.59.17 returns at oshb:Isa.60.18 (sweep: 8 verses book-wide, skeleton tier). Verified true: the mark disclosure is byte-correct — setumah attached to MT 59:21 (break after that verse, this row's close) and no other mark, paseq, or ketiv/qere object inside MT 59:15-59:21.

items.claim: The boundary itself is byte-sound, but four checkable defects sit in its evidence: the title count is the documented plene-only miss, the closing 'recognition-formula' recurrence is byte-false and untier-labeled, a span-internal paseq at the very verse the row argues is undisclosed, and the ketiv/qere gloss covers only one of the two staged forms.
items.evidence: Count-object: the plene spelling of the title stands in exactly 24 verses (sweep: 24 verses, skeleton tier), but the same title also stands defectively as קְדֹ֥שׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל at oshb:Isa.49.7 (byte tier), giving 25 title verses (12 in chs 1-39, 13 in chs 40-66); the row's twenty-four is precisely what a plene-only needle returns. Both in-span sites it names are genuine title verses — וְלִקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל at oshb:Isa.60.9 and קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל at oshb:Isa.60.14 (byte tier). Recurrence: oshb:Isa.60.16 carries the full recognition formula וְיָדַ֗עַתְּ כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ מֽוֹשִׁיעֵ֔ךְ, while oshb:Isa.60.22 carries אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה בְּעִתָּ֥הּ אֲחִישֶֽׁנָּה (both byte tier) with no knowing-verb at all; the only shared run is the two-token self-declaration, which stands in 22 verses book-wide (sweep: 22 verses, skeleton tier). So the two ends are not the same object, the recurrence carries no tier label, and the rejected alternative is built on an echo that the bytes do not support as stated. Disclosure symmetry: the row engages the mark layer at both edges (setumah attached to MT 59:21 and to MT 60:22 — both byte-correct against the single-witness inventory) and the ketiv/qere at MT 60:21, but the same inventory records a paseq seg at MT 60:9, the very verse the row argues in prose, and that object is not disclosed; the ketiv/qere engagement also omits the single-witness label. Ketiv/qere gloss: the staged pair is מטעו מַטָּעַ֛י (oshb:Isa.60.21, byte tier) — an unpointed ketiv with a third-person masculine singular suffix against a pointed qere with a first-person singular suffix. That is a suffix-person difference, not the number alternation the row's gloss offers, so 'read either way' is asserted while only one of the two forms is actually rendered. Verified true and strong: the feminine-singular address is byte-continuous across MT 60:1-60:22, from ק֥וּמִי א֖וֹרִי to the suffixed form opening oshb:Isa.60.21; oshb:Isa.61.1 carries no feminine-singular form; and the forward catchword the row does disclose is real — לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר is byte-identical at exactly oshb:Isa.60.21 and oshb:Isa.61.3 (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier) beside the shared planting root.
